tldr: AgentClinic is introduced as a multimodal agent benchmark for evaluating LLMs in interactive, dialogue-driven clinical simulations, revealing that sequential decision-making diagnostic accuracy can drop to below a tenth of static MedQA accuracy. Claude-3.5-Sonnet outperforms other LLMs across most settings, but agents vary drastically in their ability to benefit from tools like notebooks, with Llama-3 showing up to 92% relative improvement.
contributions: An interactive, dialogue-driven sequential decision-making benchmark for medical diagnosis, moving beyond static multiple-choice QA
A system incorporating 24 cognitive and implicit biases into patient and doctor agents, showing how biases affect diagnostic accuracy and patient perception
Patient agents built from real clinical sources (USMLE, MIMIC-IV, NEJM case challenges) across 9 medical specialties and 7 languages
Tool-use evaluation for doctor agents including web browsing, textbook access, reflection cycles, and persistent notebook writing
methods: AgentClinic uses four language agents (patient, doctor, measurement, moderator) each with unique instructions and information. Cases are sourced from USMLE diagnostic questions, deidentified electronic health records (MIMIC-IV), and NEJM case challenges, populated into structured JSON and manually validated with GPT-4. Doctor agents perform up to N=20 patient and measurement interactions before diagnosing. The benchmark covers 9 medical specialties and 7 languages (English, Chinese, French, Spanish, Hindi, Persian, Korean), with 24 biases introduced via system prompts. Bias effects are measured on both diagnostic accuracy and patient-centric metrics (confidence, compliance, consultation ratings).
results: On AgentClinic-MedQA: Claude-3.5 achieved 62.1%±3.3, OpenBioLLM-70B 58.3%±4.2, human physicians 54%±28.5, GPT-4 51.6%±3.3, Llama 2 70B-chat 4.5%±1.3. On AgentClinic-MIMIC-IV: Claude-3.5 scored 42.9%±3.3 vs GPT-4 at 34.0%±3.1. MedQA accuracy was only weakly predictive of AgentClinic-MedQA accuracy. Reducing interactions from N=20 to N=10 decreased accuracy from 52% to 25%. Llama-3 showed up to 92% relative improvement with the notebook tool. GPT-4's accuracy dropped minimally under bias (max 4% absolute, avg 1.5%), while Mixtral-8x7B dropped substantially (implicit bias: 37% to 32.7%). Implicit biases profoundly affected patient perception scores, with education bias consistently reducing confidence, compliance, and consultation ratings across all categories.
limitations: MedQA accuracy is only weakly predictive of sequential diagnostic performance, suggesting prior benchmarks incompletely capture clinical reasoning ability
GPT-4 sometimes refuses to execute bias instructions (25 occurrences out of 215 dialogues with gender bias), limiting its utility for studying bias effects
Patient agents are simulated by language models and may not fully capture real human patient complexity, so confidence/compliance/consultation ratings may not perfectly reflect real-world perceptions
Some models demonstrated decreased accuracy when given tools rather than improvement
